facility: Southwest Water Reclamation Facility (SWWRF), St. Petersburg, Florida
source: Brown and Caldwell for the City of St. Petersburg, SWWRF Wet Weather and Liquid Process Capacity Assessment, Final Report, July 2014 (public record)
question: The City will divert Albert Whitted's flow to the Southwest WRF, and the projected peak wet weather flow is 69 MGD. Using the hydraulic profile (Figure 5-1, water surfaces modelled at 20 and 40 MGD) and the facility data, what is the plant's hydraulic capacity today (the flow at which a tank first overtops its wall), which structure limits it, which hydraulic elements fail at 69 MGD, and what modifications or flow management would let the plant handle the 69 MGD peak?

criteria.name: Study target - future peak wet weather (peak hour) influent to SWWRF after AWWRF diversion
criteria.source: p.22 Table 3-3; p.29 Sec 5.2; question statement 69 MGD
criteria.value: 69.0 MGD Peak Hour influent (52.6 MGD Max Day, 31.4 MGD Max Month, 20.0 MGD Annual Average)

criteria.name: Hydraulic capacity definition
criteria.value: flow at which wastewater would overtopple the top of wall for that tank

criteria.name: Hydraulic profile basis - modelled flows shown on Figure 5-1
criteria.source: p.29 Sec 5.2; question statement; dwg p.30 title
criteria.value: water surfaces modelled at 20 and 40 MGD after Biosolids to Energy improvements; 40 MGD not hydraulically challenged

criteria.name: Reported hydraulic capacity and limiting unit (to be verified by re-model in later steps)
Profile conservatism - flow path
criteria.value: most conservative path excluding old plant: through secondary clarifier #3 (higher V-notch weir than #1 and #2) and northern-most filter (longest path)

criteria.name: Profile conservatism - filter level
criteria.value: hydraulic elevation in filters maintained at filter overflow elevation 115.3 feet to represent blinded filters

criteria.name: Profile RAS assumption
criteria.value: RAS flowrate 20 MGD used in profile model

criteria.name: Wet-weather loading assumption for process capacity
criteria.value: pollutant loadings during wet weather similar to dry weather loadings (dilution, concentrations drop below 80 mg/L CBOD5/TSS at peak)

criteria.name: Basis of 69 MGD projection
criteria.value: 25.5 MGD max dry weather flow + 43.2 MGD max storm contribution = 68.7 MGD rounded to 69.0 MGD peak hour

rfi.issue: Drawing elevations not legible in available record: read_drawing text truncated and p.30 text page contains title only; individual structure inverts, weir crests, top-of-wall and 20/40 MGD water surfaces not captured
rfi.reason: needed to set limits and calibrate profile; without them later steps cannot quote (dwg p.30) values
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: adopt filter overflow 115.3 ft (p.28) as the only confirmed drawing level; treat all other (dwg p.30) elevations/water surfaces as single-read unconfirmed until a legible Figure 5-1 is provided, and verify the 40.5 MGD filters limit by re-model (profile_capacity). Reason: avoids inventing elevations silently while preserving the one surveyed level the text confirms.

rfi.issue: Top-of-wall (overtopping) elevations for each tank not stated in available text pages
rfi.reason: capacity definition requires top-of-wall per tank (p.29) to find first overtopping flow
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: in later modelling place each limit from the drawing top-of-wall where legible (dwg p.30), otherwise from the 40 MGD water surface + freeboard shown on Figure 5-1; report the binding limit as filters at 40.5 MGD per p.29 until independently confirmed. Reason: follows the document's stated definition and reported result without inventing walls.

rfi.issue: New primary clarifiers, splitter boxes, cutthroat flumes, step-feed/contact-stabilization weirs: no dimensions, weir lengths, or invert data in available pages
rfi.reason: required for run_profile gravity elements between headworks and aeration basins
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: model primary/step-feed reach with the flow-meter fix only (30-in out, 48-in in per p.28) and literature weir/flume coefficients; note primary dimensions as TBD pending Biosolids-to-Energy Engineering Report. Reason: text confirms the meter was the restriction and flumes pass peak unsubmerged, so meter change is the only quantifiable change available.

rfi.issue: Pipe bottlenecks list gives diameter only (54-in, 24-in, 48-in, 48-in) with no length, slope, roughness, or invert
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: in later steps use as-built lengths/inverts if on Figure 5-1 (dwg p.30) where legible, otherwise standard roughness with lengths scaled from plant layout and flag as ASSUMPTION. Reason: diameter-only data from p.29 is insufficient for independent hydraulics; labelling preserves traceability.

rfi.issue: RAS 20 MGD constant vs variable with influent; RAS + influent vs influent-only flow through downstream units unclear
rfi.reason: affects aeration-to-filters hydraulics at 20-69 MGD influent
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: hold RAS at 20 MGD as stated on dwg p.30 for all profile runs (20, 40.5, 69 MGD influent) unless text directs otherwise, and quote total flow to downstream units as influent + RAS where applicable. Reason: follows the drawing note explicitly.

rfi.issue: Effluent disposal split: effluent pumping 39.6 MGD (5 pumps) + deep wells 27 MGD = 66.6 MGD combined, less than 69 MGD peak; reclaimed storage 5 MG + 10 MG operating rules not given
rfi.reason: determines whether CCB tailwater controls upstream grade at 69 MGD
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: treat effluent pumping + deep wells as firm-capacity check (largest pump out of service) and reclaimed storage as equalization; flag any shortfall to 69 MGD as flow-management need. Reason: Table 2-1 (p.13) gives only ratings, not firm capacity or operating logic.

rfi.issue: Old-plant aeration (0.65 MG) and clarifiers (0.64 MG) status: text says aeration modifications allowed decommissioning old plant while maintaining 20-MGD permitted capacity, but model says excluding old plant
rfi.item: Old plant in service or not
rfi.reason: affects units_on_path and firm capacity counting
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: exclude old-plant basins/clarifiers from the hydraulic path (most conservative, per p.28) but retain them as standby for flow-management discussion. Reason: matches the modelled conservative path while acknowledging the permitted-capacity statement on p.10.

rfi.issue: 68.7 MGD (25.5+43.2 on p.20) vs 69.0 MGD Peak Hour (Table 3-3 on p.22) discrepancy
rfi.reason: 0.3 MGD difference affects pass/fail at the margin
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: adopt 69.0 MGD as the design peak (Table 3-3 governs) and note 68.7 MGD as the derivation. Reason: Table 3-3 is the adopted wet-weather basis of design.

alternatives.cost_basis: New parallel 48-in and 54-in yard piping (~hundreds of ft) + CCB weir-channel widening + filter effluent improvements; unit-cost per ft-diameter plus structures. ASSUMPTION: no land/permitting included.
alternatives.option: Alt A - Parallel relief sewers (second 54-in Filters-CCB, second 48-in Sec-Filters and Aer-Sec) + doubled CCB weir length
alternatives.result: SW_altA_par at 69 MGD: P54 HGL 108.37 ft margin +6.93 ft, Sec reach 115.55 ft margin +5.09 ft, Aer reach 118.66 ft margin +6.34 ft (velocities halved by share 0.5). Headworks lumped still 146.75 ft margin -11.33 ft, so downstream fix alone FAILS 69 MGD without headworks/primary fix.

alternatives.cost_basis: Use existing third flow path to contact stabilization with manual overflow weir gate (p.29 Sec 5) + primary bypass logic + 15 MG reclaimed storage (5+10 MG p.13) to shave 2-hr >60 MGD peak (0.01% probability p.19); chlorination of bypass per permit. ASSUMPTION: permit allows primary-treated bypass blending for <1-day storm with dilute loads (p.21 Sec 3.3).
alternatives.option: Alt B - Cap filtered/secondary path at ~40 MGD; bypass primary-treated excess (~29 MGD at 69 MGD peak) around secondary/filters to CCB/effluent via existing contact-stabilization/bypass; equalize with 15 MG storage; retain old plant (2x65-ft aeration 0.65 MG + 2x65-ft clarifiers 0.64 MG p.13) as standby
alternatives.result: By definition downstream sees 40 MGD which per p.29 and SW_base40 is not hydraulically challenged (filters at 115.3 ft, no overtop). SW_altB_bypass full-69-through-filters run confirms without bypass margins -10.58/-2.48/-2.63 ft, so bypass is required. Short storm (<1 day p.19) + dilute loads (p.21) + 66.6 MGD disposal (39.6+27 p.13) +15 MG storage makes 69 MGD manageable.

alternatives.cost_basis: Filter rehabilitation/backwash control to lower operating level below blinded 115.3 ft (p.28) + weir/channel work; single-structure rehab. ASSUMPTION: operating HGL can be held 1-2 ft below overflow with clean media.

notes: ELEVATIONS OF EXISTING STRUCTURES BASED UPON SURVEY PERFORMED BY McKIM & CREED, OCTOBER 2013.
PROFILE WAS MODELED USING A RAS FLOWRATE OF 20 MGD.
PRIMARY CLARIFIERS HAVE A PEAK CAPACITY OF 40 MGD. INFLUENT FLOWS BEYOND THIS AMOUNT WILL BE BYPASSED AROUND THE PRIMARY CLARIFIERS.
AT FLOWS GREATER THAN 40 MGD, 29 MGD WILL BE SENT TO THE FRONT OF THE AERATION BASINS, WITH THE REMAINDER BEING SENT TO A COMBINATION OF THE STEP FEED AND CONTACT STABILIZATION FEED POINTS.

THE 69 MGD PROFILE IS BASED UPON A FIXED HYDRAULIC GRADE OF 122.92 IN THE AERATION BASINS AND IS MODELED UPSTREAM TO THE PROPOSED TIE-IN POINT OF THIS PROJECT. ADDITIONAL MODIFICATIONS ARE NEEDED TO PASS THESE FLOWS UPSTREAM AND DOWNSTREAM OF THE MODELED PORTION OF THE FACILITY.
